title: 06 · Training the AOT cache with a real workload
question: A more complex application needs warming up with different pieces of code exercised. How do you train the AOT cache with a real workload when the real Config Server, Vault and Mongo can't be reached at build time, and what does it buy over training on startup alone?

answer.pass: Three images of the same app are compared: UNTRAINED has no AOT cache; CONTEXT-TRAINED has a cache recorded in docker build by only starting the app (the Spring context comes up, then the JVM exits before any request), so it holds startup code only; WORKLOAD-TRAINED has a cache recorded in the pipeline while the app served real requests (training-pipeline.sh), so it also holds the request-path code. Result: Train in the pipeline, not in docker build: run the untrained image against throwaway Config Server, Vault and Mongo with fake data, drive a representative workload at it, stop it cleanly (the JVM writes the cache on exit), and add only that cache file on top of the exact untrained image. Startup stays about the same as a cache trained on startup alone, but the first requests no longer pay for loading and profiling the request path: the first request is about twice as fast and the first 300 requests are 10-20% faster, and far fewer classes are loaded from the jars at runtime. The same workload-trained image then ran as dev1 (dev,dev1) and prod1 (prod,prod1), each with its own Config Server settings, Vault secret, database and JVM flags, and both used the AOT cache.
answer.fail: Three images of the same app are compared: UNTRAINED has no AOT cache; CONTEXT-TRAINED has a cache recorded in docker build by only starting the app (the Spring context comes up, then the JVM exits before any request), so it holds startup code only; WORKLOAD-TRAINED has a cache recorded in the pipeline while the app served real requests (training-pipeline.sh), so it also holds the request-path code. Not as expected: at least one result differs from the known behaviour. See 'Unexpected results' for what differed and what to check.
answer.inconclusive: Three images of the same app are compared: UNTRAINED has no AOT cache; CONTEXT-TRAINED has a cache recorded in docker build by only starting the app (the Spring context comes up, then the JVM exits before any request), so it holds startup code only; WORKLOAD-TRAINED has a cache recorded in the pipeline while the app served real requests (training-pipeline.sh), so it also holds the request-path code. The training worked, but some timings varied too much (or had too few runs) to judge. Close other workloads and rerun with more runs (make examples EX=06 RUNS=5).

tested: The training pipeline (training-pipeline.sh): build the untrained image, start throwaway Config Server / Vault / Mongo with fake data, run the untrained image with -XX:AOTCacheOutput, drive 3,000 mixed requests (8 in parallel), stop it with SIGTERM, and build the final image as the untrained image plus app.aot.

Two environments, with this example's own Config Server, Vault and Mongo (compose.yml): dev1 (profiles dev,dev1, its own JVM flags with a smaller heap) and prod1 (profiles prod,prod1, the image's default flags, i.e. the ones the caches were trained with). Each gets tier settings (workload-app-dev.yml / -prod.yml) and environment settings (workload-app-dev1.yml / -prod1.yml) from Config Server, and its own Mongo password from Vault.
Three images of the same app timed in dev1: no cache, a cache trained on startup only (in the build), a cache trained by the workload.

Per image, RUNS fresh starts (round-robin, Mongo data reset before each): Spring's startup time, the latency of the first request, and the total time of the first 50 and the first 300 requests of the same fixed request mix.
Per image, one run with class-load logging across startup + 300 requests: how many classes came from the AOT cache and how many had to be loaded from the jars.

The workload-trained image (the one you'd ship) deployed to dev1 and to prod1: profiles, which Config Server files and Vault path it loaded, its database, a per-tier setting, its JVM flags, and whether it used the AOT cache.

training.started.label: untrained image started against the throwaway services
training.started.why: The training stack has the same kinds of services as every environment, with fake data and credentials from bootstrap.sh.
ifUnexpected: Read raw/training.log.
Did aot-06-config-server:1.0.0 build? (docker compose -f training/compose.yml build config-server)

training.workload.label: training workload
training.workload.why: run-workload.sh drives the same request mix as prod traffic (creates, queries, aggregation, status updates, invalid requests).
ifUnexpected: Read raw/training.log for exceptions during the workload.
Run ./run-workload.sh against a running instance to see the failing request.

training.cache-written.label: app.aot after a clean stop
training.cache-written.why: With -XX:AOTCacheOutput the JVM records what ran and, when it exits normally, assembles the cache in a child JVM. 'docker compose stop trainer' sends SIGTERM: Spring shuts down gracefully and the JVM exits normally; the trainer's stop_grace_period (300s) leaves time for the assembly.
ifUnexpected: Was the trainer killed (exit 137) before the assembly finished? Raise stop_grace_period in training/compose.yml.
Look for 'AOTCache creation is complete' in raw/training.log.

training.final-image.label: final image layers
training.final-image.why: The cache is only valid for the exact JDK and /app files it was trained with, so the final image is FROM the untrained image and adds nothing but app.aot. No training data, secrets or tools end up in it.
ifUnexpected: Check Dockerfile.trained: FROM ${BASE} + COPY app.aot only.
raw/final-image-history.txt shows the top layers.

training.cache-size.label: AOT cache size
training.cache-size.why: The workload-trained cache also holds the request-path classes and the method profiles recorded during the workload.

training.pipeline.label: training pipeline ran to the end
training.pipeline.why: Everything after training measures the three images training-pipeline.sh builds. If it stops early there is nothing to measure, so the demo reports what the pipeline recorded and stops.
ifUnexpected: The training checks above show which step failed (raw/training.log has the trainer's log).
No other training check failed? Then a docker build or a docker compose command failed: rerun the pipeline on its own (make -C examples/06-training-workload train) to see its output.

cache.untrained.label: untrained: AOT cache
cache.untrained.why: Reference: this image has no cache file, so everything is loaded from the jars.

cache.context.label: context-trained: AOT cache
cache.context.why: The build-time cache covers the classes loaded during startup.
ifUnexpected: Rebuild: make -C examples/06-training-workload image

cache.workload.label: workload-trained: AOT cache
cache.workload.why: Trained with the same JDK and /app layers (the untrained image), so the cache is valid.
ifUnexpected: Was the final image built FROM the same untrained image that was trained? Check training.final-image.
Read raw/workload.classes.txt.

outside.untrained.label: untrained: classes loaded from the jars

outside.context.label: context-trained: classes loaded from the jars
outside.context.why: Information: the request path (validation, JSON, Mongo queries, error handling) wasn't seen during startup-only training.

outside.workload.label: workload-trained: classes loaded from the jars
outside.workload.why: Information: what the workload didn't exercise.

fewer-outside.label: workload training leaves fewer classes to load from the jars
fewer-outside.why: The workload exercised the request paths during training, so their classes are in the cache instead of being loaded on the first requests.
ifUnexpected: Does run-workload.sh exercise the same endpoints as the measurement? Compare the status counts in the training output.
Read raw/context.classes.txt and raw/workload.classes.txt.

env.started.label: started
env.started.why: The same image, started with this environment's env vars and Vault token.
ifUnexpected: Read the environment's failed-start log in the evidence.
Was the environment bootstrapped? (examples/06-training-workload/.secrets/<env>.env)

env.profiles.label: profiles
ifUnexpected: Check start_app in demo.sh passes APP_ENV / APP_ENV_INDEX for this environment.

env.config-files.label: Config Server files (most specific first)
env.config-files.why: Config Server serves the files for the active profiles: the environment file (-dev1 / -prod1), then the tier file (-dev / -prod), then the shared file. Most specific wins.
ifUnexpected: Check the files exist in examples/06-training-workload/config-repo (workload-app.yml, -dev.yml, -dev1.yml, -prod.yml, -prod1.yml).

env.tier-setting.label: app.orders.max-page-size (tier setting)
env.tier-setting.why: Set per tier by Config Server (50 in dev, 100 in prod) and used by the orders endpoint, not baked into the image.
ifUnexpected: Check workload-app-dev.yml / workload-app-prod.yml in examples/06-training-workload/config-repo.

env.mongo-db.label: Mongo database (from Config Server)
env.mongo-db.why: Each environment has its own database and user, from its environment file.
ifUnexpected: Check workload-app-<env>.yml in examples/06-training-workload/config-repo.

env.vault.label: Vault path loaded
env.vault.why: Each environment's token can only read its own path; the Mongo password comes from there.
ifUnexpected: Rerun the bootstrap: examples/06-training-workload/bootstrap.sh dev1 prod1

env.mongo-ping.label: Mongo accepted the password from Vault
env.mongo-ping.why: The password only exists in Vault and Mongo; the app read it at startup.
ifUnexpected: Rerun the bootstrap: examples/06-training-workload/bootstrap.sh dev1 prod1

env.cache.label: AOT cache used
env.cache.why: dev1's flags (smaller heap) and prod1's flags (the training flags) are both compatible with the cache (example 01).
ifUnexpected: Read the environment's classes file in the evidence.
Did someone give the environment an incompatible flag (e.g. ZGC on JDK 25)?

env.jvm.label: JVM flags
env.jvm.why: Information: each environment's own flags; prod1 runs the image default.

env.timing.label: startup and first request
env.timing.why: Information: one start in this environment, with class-load logging on.

env.same-image.label: distinct images across dev1 and prod1
env.same-image.why: One build for every environment (example 04): the environment only changes env vars and fetched settings.
ifUnexpected: Check start_app runs workload-app:workload-trained for both environments.

startup.context.label: context-trained
startup.context.why: The build-time cache covers startup, which is what it was trained on.

startup.workload.label: workload-trained
startup.workload.why: Startup is covered by both caches. The workload cache also preloads the request-path classes at startup, which costs a little time but not much.

first.context.label: context-trained
first.context.why: Information: the startup-only cache doesn't cover the request path, so the first request still loads validation, JSON and Mongo classes.

early.context.label: context-trained
early.context.why: Information: the startup-only cache leaves the request path to be loaded and profiled during these first requests.

first.workload.label: workload-trained
first.workload.why: The request path's classes come from the cache, so the first request doesn't have to load them.
ifUnexpected: Check fewer-outside: did the workload cache really cover the request path?
Rerun with more runs: RUNS=5.

early.workload.label: workload-trained
early.workload.why: Information only: across runs this ranged from 10% to 1.7× faster. The reliable gain is ~30 ms on the very first request; spread over 50 requests (~0.2 s in total) that is within run-to-run noise, so it isn't judged.

warmup.context.label: context-trained
warmup.context.why: Information: the startup-only cache helps little once requests arrive.

warmup.workload.label: workload-trained
warmup.workload.why: Still faster over 300 requests, but the gain is diluted: it is concentrated in the first requests, and later requests run equally fast with either cache, so this is judged with a tighter ±10% band.
ifUnexpected: Rerun with more runs: RUNS=5.
Is the measurement mix the same as the training mix? (run-workload.sh, same seed)

reproduce: make examples EX=06                                 # train + measure + report
make -C examples/06-training-workload train         # only the training pipeline -> workload-app:workload-trained
make -C examples/06-training-workload demo RUNS=5   # more starts per image
